requirement: The trust engine shall raise AMBER within 3 s of total GNSS loss (proposal)
notes: 12 GNSS-off runs: time to detect 1.0 to 1.4 s (simulation)

requirement: The trust engine shall not leave GREEN in nominal runs
notes: 9 nominal runs, no alert after startup (simulation)

requirement: The displayed bound shall contain the true position error in at least 95% of GREEN epochs
notes: Only since the calibrated bound (PR 37): before it the console's bound held in 30.8% of reports

requirement: No vehicle command shall execute without a recorded operator approval, except PX4's own failsafes
notes: The gate is the only path to a command; an AST test enforces it

requirement: On RED the system shall propose re-assignment of the vehicle's remaining sectors within 2 s
notes: Measured in 6 live three-vehicle runs: 5 to 6 ms from the backend receiving the RED report to the recommendation. Excludes the engine's report interval (2 Hz, so up to 0.5 s by design) and delivery to the console, which were not measured

requirement: Every alert shall show a reason code an operator can act on
notes: Text review done and tested for every recommendation the recommender can make; one gap fixed (what happens to a vehicle with no command). Whether an operator acts on it is not shown: round 1 participants did not act unaided; round 2 pending

requirement: The operator can see all vehicles' trust states without scrolling at 1080p
notes: Measured at 1920 x 1080: rows are 189 px and 5 vehicles fit with the decision band showing, nothing scrolls (the spec says 3 to 5)

requirement: Time to detect: GNSS degradation onset to AMBER or RED, median under 3 s (proposal)
notes: Met for GNSS off and wrong fix; a frozen position takes 3.0 to 4.5 s, above the target

requirement: False alert rate: 0 in N nominal runs
notes: 0 in 9 nominal runs; 1 episode in 1.73 flight hours over all runs (a simulation stall, see the held-out report)

requirement: Misleading-trust epochs under 1%: true error above the displayed bound while GREEN
notes: Since the calibrated bound; with the old bound most GREEN reports were misleading

requirement: Mission completion: at least 90% of the area covered in a single-vehicle-loss scenario
notes: Simulation, three vehicles, one lost (a long GNSS outage that makes PX4 land it), scripted operator approving after 15 s: 100% of the area covered in 3 of 3 runs. With the operator denying: 87% in 3 of 3 runs (the lost vehicle's sector 62%), so the re-task is what meets the target. One loss pattern, few runs, scripted operator

requirement: Operator workload proxy: alerts plus approvals per 10 minutes
notes: Reported: single-vehicle runs 3.07 interruptions per 10 min (frozen position) and 6.91 (long outage) of flight, 0 in nominal; fleet runs 1.9 (approved) and 2.8 (denied) alerts plus decisions per 10 min. The operator is scripted, so this counts the system's demands, not a person's effort

requirement: Time to decision: alert shown to operator approval
notes: Round 1, protocol v1, N=2: P1 approved 134.9 s after the first alert and only after a hint; P2 did not decide. Redesign and protocol v2 not yet re-tested
